_comment: Sweep routers (#693/PR #711): a lone player Cavalry ('Sweeper', uid 0) sits between two enemy targets. 'Holdout' (uid 3) is a full-strength Infantry that closes on a player Spearmen tie-down ('Anvil') and stays FIGHTING it -- close to the sweeper (~140-150 px) but never routs. 'Fleeing' (uid 4) is a weak, low-morale Infantry spawned in contact with a second player Cavalry ('Breaker'); it takes until ~tick 50 to cross the rout threshold (its starting morale is low but not zero), then ROUTS and flees. Giving the sweeper the SWEEP_ROUTERS stance (Ctrl+,) makes it lock onto Holdout at first (nothing is routing yet), then switch onto Fleeing the moment it starts routing (~tick 55-60), bypassing the closer, still-fighting Holdout -- the actual re-targeting choice under test. Because Breaker keeps pursuing under its own Hold order, Fleeing is run down and fully annihilated by ~tick 85-90, at which point the sweeper reverts to Holdout (the only enemy left in range) for the remainder of the run. Verified by state dump: target_enemy_uid is null at tick 10, 3 (Holdout) at tick 40, 4 (Fleeing) at tick 70 -- inside the router-priority window -- then 3 again from tick 100 onward once Fleeing is gone.

shape_residual.reason: Uid 4's drift is tracked in #1847: a block marching with its grid folded across its facing lets its men drift off their slots. Uid 4 (the 30-man unit meant to rout) marches with its grid about 100 degrees from its facing and its motion 98 to 110 degrees off the grid, and its residual climbs about 0.17 to 0.2 wu a tick from tick 180 on both trees: on main 2c2955cc from 4.45 wu at tick 180 to 17.74 at 260, on branch ed307f22 from 4.18 to 19.92. On main uid 4 reads engaged, which the scan exempts, for most of ticks 170 to 260, and on the branch it does not, because with flank and rear contact at the defender's edge (#1845) the Spearmen (uid 1), spawned 10 wu from team 1's Infantry (uid 3) on its flank, part to the flank's edge in the first ticks, so the clip diverges from tick 1 and uid 4 marches after a different target. The clip itself needs re-staging (#1753: it no longer shows a router or a retarget). Measured 2026-10-22 with 2-tick samples from tick 2: branch ed307f22 fails on the clip seed and perturbed seeds 1 to 4 (19.9, 20.1, 19.0, 19.3 and 15.0 wu against the 13.5 wu threshold), main on none. With #1792 (main f12d083f) the clip diverges from ac16177f at tick 119, at #1792's own fold: there uid 4, in contact with team 0's second Cavalry (uid 2) whose centre is inside its footprint, folds small re-faces into its formation instead of turning its grid, and on dense 2-tick FULL dumps from tick 2, judged with no exemption against 13.5, uid 4's worst reads ac16177f 19.3, 17.0, 17.5, 20.9 and a pass on seeds 0 to 4, and f12d083f 20.1, 20.9, 23.1, 21.6, 14.9. #1859 now squares that absorbed part on its own whenever the block is out of contact, and the worst reads 22.2, 17.0, 18.1, 22.0, 19.8 (8b49922d). Squaring it recovers little of the rise over ac16177f, because the rise accrues while the block is still in and out of the fight and the residual is fitted after a rotation, so a grid turned off its men costs it nothing directly: at tick 180 the residual reads ac16177f 12.6, 11.4, 12.9, 12.3, 9.7, f12d083f 14.5, 13.2, 14.3, 14.0, 11.7 and 8b49922d 13.7, 12.9, 14.2, 13.5, 11.5. Much of the seed-to-seed swing past tick 180 comes from an order the AI re-issues at tick 182: once the block is clear, its re-square (#1852) squares the whole fold, which sits either side of a quarter-turn, reflecting it by a half-turn on one side and not the other (#1865). On seed 0 it runs at tick 199 on a fold of -85.6 degrees on f12d083f (no reflection) and -91.0 with #1859 (reflected, leaving 89.0 degrees to turn out). On seed 4 f12d083f's 14.9 is lower only because uid 4 reads engaged, which the scan exempts, from tick 204; its residual is higher than #1859's at every sample from tick 150. Overlap, which this exemption does not cover, fails on seed 3 on all three trees (ac16177f 1.65, f12d083f 2.21, #1859 0.21). Measured 2026-10-25 on Windows. The excess over ac16177f that remains is the block leaving the melee scrambled and marching on so (#1837) on top of the #1847 drift, and the re-square flip (#1865); remove this exemption once all three have landed.
